name: a-keyed-hint-stands-the-same-height-as-a-plain-one
description: the hint card used to take the height of its tallest child, so a bubble carrying a keycap stood a few pixels taller than a text-only one beside it. This run brings up the floating address bar, hovers the copy link button to raise a keyed hint on the shared /hint overlay, measures it, then pushes a plain hint through the same document and measures that. The shim has no engine, so this is the only place the two boxes are really laid out.

actions.note: ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
Developer Mode: the floating address bar carries the copy link button

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.dvcopy'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerover', {bubbles: true})); return 'hovered'; })()

actions.note: the devbar route sends its hint through chrome.send to HintOverlayWidget's own /hint document

actions.expression: (() => { const box = () => document.querySelector('.hint').getBoundingClientRect().height; const keyed = Math.round(box()); window.atriumShowHint({text: 'Copy URL'}); const plain = Math.round(box()); return keyed + '/' + plain; })()
actions.note: atriumShowHint is the push installHintOverlay wires, so the plain bubble is built by the same code path the native one is
the first stream in a run can deliver no frames

assertions.desc: setup: the devbar came up with its copy link button
setup: the copy link button was found and hovered
setup: the raised hint carries a keycap
A keyed bubble and a plain one stand at the one card height
